narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the prose frame and introduces each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: Upright man of Hus, father of ten grown children, stricken and lamenting.

2.t: Indeed I know it is so, and that man cannot be justified, compared with God.

3.t: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand.

4.t: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath resisted him, and hath had peace?

5.t: Who hath removed mountains, and they whom he overthrew in his wrath, knew it not.

6.t: Who shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

7.t: Who commandeth the sun, and it riseth not: and shutteth up the stars, as it were, under a seal:

8.t: Who alone spreadeth out the heavens, and walketh upon the waves of the sea.

9.t: Who maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and Hyades, and the inner parts of the south.

10.t: Who doth things great and incomprehensible, and wonderful, of which there is no number.

11.t: If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart, I shall not understand.

12.t: If he examine on a sudden, who shall answer him? or who can say: Why dost thou so?

13.t: God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world.

14.t: What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?

15.t: I, who although I should have any just thing, would not answer, but would make supplication to my judge.

16.t: And if he should hear me when I call, I should not believe that he had heard my voice.

17.t: For he shall crush me in a whirlwind, and multiply my wounds even without cause.

18.t: He alloweth not my spirit to rest, and he filleth me with bitterness.

19.t: If strength be demanded, he is most strong: if equity of judgment, no man dare bear witness for me.

20.t: If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me: if I would shew myself innocent, he shall prove me wicked.

21.t: Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of, and I shall be weary of my life.

22.t: One thing there is that I have spoken, both the innocent and the wicked he consumeth.

23.t: If he scourge, let him kill at once, and not laugh at the pains of the innocent.

24.t: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, he covereth the face of the judges thereof: and if it be not he, who is it then?

25.t: My days have been swifter than a post: they have fled away and have not seen good.

26.t: They have passed by as ships carrying fruits, as an eagle flying to the prey.

27.t: If I say: I will not speak so: I change my face, and am tormented with sorrow.

28.t: I feared all my works, knowing that thou didst not spare the offender.

29.t: But if so also I am wicked, why have I laboured in vain?

30.t: If I be washed, as it were, with snow waters, and my hands shall shine ever so clean:

31.t: Yet thou shalt plunge me in filth, and my garments shall abhor me.

32.t: For I shall not answer a man that is like myself: nor one that may be heard with me equally in judgment.

33.t: There is none that may be able to reprove both, and to put his hand between both.

34.t: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me.

35.t: I will speak, and will not fear him: for I cannot answer while I am in fear.
